value.reason: server.ts:638 registers a GET handler for /rest/user/security-question, and routes/securityQuestion.ts:13 reads the email address from the query string (`const email = query.email`). The frontend service (security-question.service.ts:25) builds the request by appending `?email=` plus the user's email to the URL, so the email always travels in the URL. server.ts:370 turns on Morgan in 'combined' format with an access log stream. That format records the full request URL, query string included, so every user's email is written in plain text to logs/access.log.%DATE% and kept for 2 days. This is the positive example's pattern: personal contact data sent in a GET query string (CWE-598) and then stored in logs with no masking or obfuscation. It falls short of the reasonable security safeguards required for personal data. Rule 6(1)(a) names masking and obfuscation as such safeguards. The negative example is different: it sends the email in a POST body and keeps only non-personal data like `page` in the query.
